ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transactions Reports Act (Act No. 3636, as amended), Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information (Act No. 6516, as amended), and the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information; Supreme Court Registration of Commercial Names under the Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended); Beneficial Ownership disclosure obligations under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information Article 2(3) and the Financial Services Commission's Beneficial Ownership Reporting Guidelines (effective November 1, 2024, aligned with PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 in China but implemented through KoFIU and registry data held by the Supreme Court); Real Name Financial Transactions Act (Act No. 5493, as amended).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (法人登記簿謄本)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the Supreme Court of Korea (local court registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for apostille convention countries; non-apostille countries must undergo Korean consular legalization at the Korean embassy/consulate in the country of origin; do not chain apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (해당없음 - Korean registry extracts are contemporaneous; certified true copy issued by the court registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local District Court Registry Office (Supreme Court of Korea)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by RoK Ministry of Foreign Affairs for member states; consular legalization by Korean diplomatic mission for non-member states; parallel paths, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney for pre-incorporation representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public (Korean notary) and the corporate board of the founding shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille by RoK Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention jurisdictions; for non-convention jurisdictions, notarization followed by consular legalization at the Korean embassy/consulate; no hybrid chaining.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by RoK Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille states; consular legalization by Korean consular officer for non-member states; mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: International bank where the founder/primary investor maintains an account (foreign bank) or domestic Korean bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the issuing country's competent authority (if the issuing bank is in an Apostille state) or consular legalization by the Korean embassy in the issuing country (if not an Apostille state); never both.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any corporate formation step, the compliance partner must conduct enhanced due diligence on all direct and indirect shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners of KR_YUHANGHOESA against the following sources: (1) the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) consolidated assessment; (2) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (3) the U.S. OFAC SDN List, CAPTA List, and Non-SDN Consolidated Sanctions List; (4) the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list; (5) the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Korea Customs Service sanctions lists under the Trade Sanctions Regulations; (6) the Interpol and domestic law enforcement watchlists for corruption and financial crimes. The screening must also include all current and immediate former Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by FATF Recommendation 12, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and international organization PEPs, extended to immediate family members and close associates. Automated screening must be supplemented with manual negative-media and adverse-information checks through open-source intelligence (OSINT) databases and professional investigative databases. Any name or entity flagged as a match at any confidence level must be escalated to the AML Compliance Officer for heightened scrutiny, enhanced due diligence, and if necessary, termination of the engagement. For a low-risk wholesale construction materials entity, the standard rule is a risk-based diligence review completed within five business days, with an enhanced review lasting no more than 20 business days where a PEP or sanctions indicator appears. All screening results must be documented in a contemporaneous risk decision memorandum, archived for at least five years, and retained in accordance with Article 5 of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Corporate Registry (i-RO, 인터넷등기소 / www.iros.go.kr) and the Korean Company Registration Search System at the local district court registry office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be registered in Hangul (Korean script). A corresponding English transliteration may be used as an externally displayed trade name but is not a substitute for the statutory Korean name. The four-tier naming convention requires (1) a unique distinguishing element, (2) the business purpose descriptor, (3) the legal form suffix such as '유한회사' (Yuhan Hoesa), and (4) the optional English trade name. A phonetic transliteration of a foreign brand is permitted only if it does not create confusion with existing registered names. All names must comply with the Commercial Act Article 18, which prohibits using a name that is identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered company in the same jurisdiction. The registry system applies a computer-automated similarity check against all existing names in the nation, including five-character phonetic matching for Hangul transliterations. Where a Latin-alphabet name is added, it must be a direct transliteration or the official brand name of the foreign parent; any Korean-language rendering of that brand name must be clearly distinct from existing marks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended; Chapter V on Limited Liability Companies (Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 287-2 through 287-45, and Article 317 on Registration of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the Local District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the company registered office, administered by the National Court Administration of the Supreme Court of Korea; online filing via the Supreme Court I-REG e-registration system
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporation Registration (Incorporation Registration Application) together with the Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Korean Commercial Act imposes no statutory minimum stated capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. The only capital rule is that each founding member must pay the full amount of his or her subscribed contribution in cash or in kind before the incorporation registration is filed. No blocked escrow account is mandated by law. For cash contributions, the Court Registry requires a bank-issued capital deposit certificate. For in-kind contributions, an independent appraiser valuation report approved by the Court Registry is required. For the intended Portland clinker wholesale and ocean-borne trade business, the stated capital should nevertheless be sufficient to evidence creditworthiness for letters of credit, vessel charter payments, customs duties, and port terminal deposits.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. 2025-001 OF THE FOUNDING BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF KR YUHANG HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY)

WHEREAS the Company was organized as a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and is being incorporated for the wholesale trading, ocean-borne import, transshipment and distribution of Portland cement clinker and hydraulic cement; and

WHEREAS the Articles of Incorporation have been signed by all founding members and each member has agreed to subscribe to the contributory units identified in the subscription schedule; and

WHEREAS the registered office has been identified and must be formally adopted by this resolution; and

WHEREAS the opening of corporate bank accounts and the appointment of statutory officers are necessary for carrying out the initial formation filings, trade finance and daily governance of the Company.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED:

1. Adoption of Articles and Subscription of Contributory Units. The notarized Articles of Incorporation are hereby ratified and approved. The initial stated capital of the Company is set at [KRW AMOUNT], divided into [NUMBER] contributory units. The subscription schedule showing the name, number of units and contribution amount of each founding member is approved and adopted, and the Representative Director is instructed to collect each contribution in full, deposit all cash contributions into a Korean domestic bank account, obtain the capital deposit certificate required for registration, and obtain the independent appraisal report for any in-kind contribution.

2. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is hereby fixed at [FULL REGISTERED ADDRESS IN THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA]. The Representative Director is authorized to execute the office or warehouse lease in the Company name and to file the registered office notice and all related changes with the competent Local District Court Registry.

3. Banking Authorization. The Company shall maintain its principal banking relationship with [BANK NAME AND BRANCH]. The Representative Director, together with [AUTHORIZED SIGNATORY], is authorized to open operating and settlement accounts, sign account mandate cards, approve SWIFT wire transfers, execute electronic banking instructions, endorse bills of exchange, issue and settle documentary letters of credit, and transact all foreign-exchange business required for the import and wholesale distribution of bulk Portland clinker. Unless the account mandate specifies joint signature, any one authorized signatory may bind the Company in the ordinary course.

4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. [NAME] is appointed Representative Director. [NAME] is appointed Statutory Auditor if required by the Articles of Incorporation or the Commercial Act. [NAME] is appointed Manager responsible for corporate tax filings and business registration. The officers are jointly and severally authorized to complete the Court Registry incorporation filing, obtain the National Tax Service business registration, secure the Company electronic tax invoice system, file the foreign trade business report, and register the Company with Korea Customs Service.

5. Implementation and General Delegation. Any one director or appointed officer may execute all applications, verifications, powers of attorney, undertakings, contracts and ancillary documents necessary to give full legal effect to the foregoing resolutions, including engagement of Korean legal counsel and certified public accountants.

This Resolution is effective immediately and remains in force until amended, revoked or superseded by a subsequent members or directors resolution.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea; online portal: HomeTax System (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) The foreign non-resident entity must appoint a Korean tax representative (domestic withholding agent or regular tax agent) for service of process and VAT compliance. 2) Prepare and submit to the competent district tax office: articles of incorporation or equivalent foreign entity constitutive documents, evidence of foreign registration, appointment certificate of the Korean tax representative, and details of the local business address or representative's place of business. 3) File an Application for Business Registration (business registration certificate application) via the HomeTax System or in person at the district tax office; this must be done within 20 days from the commencement of any taxable supply in Korea. 4) Upon approval, the NTS issues a Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit TIN/VAT registration number; the same number is used for corporate income tax and VAT purposes. 5) If the non-resident entity has no Korean establishment but supplies cross-border services subject to VAT, a simplified foreign vendor registration is available to obtain a VAT ID; a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) with an actual Korean office must maintain full registration.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) under the Korean Value Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No statutory turnover threshold for corporations; VAT registration is mandatory upon first taxable supply of goods or services in Korea. The simplified taxpayer regime for very small entrepreneurs applies only to qualifying individual traders, not to a Yuhan Hoesa LLC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All registered VAT taxpayers must issue electronic tax invoices (ETIs) for business-to-business supplies and transmit them through the NTS HomeTax System (ETS). ETIs must be issued and sent to the NTS no later than the day following the supply date. The NTS maintains near-real-time automated cross-checking of electronic tax invoices and cash-receipt data to detect invoice fraud; there is no separate physical fiscal stamping regime but electronic invoice data submission is a mandatory statutory compliance duty. Failure to issue or transmit an ETI subjects the supplier to VAT penalties and assesses the purchaser's input tax disallowance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Korean VAT Act, the export of goods is zero-rated where the goods are actually exported from Korea, the Korean VAT payer is the exporter named in the customs export declaration, the sale is made to a foreign purchaser, and the consideration is paid in foreign currency (or under a specific foreign-exchange arrangement) and repatriated to Korea. For the current scope of portland clinker in bulk for ocean vessel freight and wholesale distribution, zero-rating is available only on documented export sales with customs exit confirmation and foreign exchange earnings substantiation. Offshore digital services likewise qualify for zero-rating when supplied exclusively to non-residents and paid for in foreign currency, but goods export is the primary applicable category under this task payload.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Electronically filed through Korean UNI-PASS export clearance system)
Bill of Lading (Ocean Bill of Lading evidencing export vessel shipment)
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent proof of foreign currency repatriation issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS will retrospectively claw back zero-rated VAT and assess 10% VAT on the export invoice amount if the required customs export declaration, ocean bill of lading, or foreign exchange repatriation evidence is missing, falsified, or inconsistent. Additional penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value Added Tax Act range from 10% (negligent underpayment) to 40% (dishonest fraud) of the assessed tax, plus daily overdue interest of 0.025% per day. Deliberate export-evidence fraud is a criminal offense carrying potential imprisonment up to three years and fines up to KRW 30,000,000.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting as the monetary and foreign exchange authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), the Financial Services Commission, and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit jointly overseeing foreign-exchange information and AML enforcement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalised but supervised convertibility regime. Current-account and most capital-account transactions are permitted under a negative-list system and may proceed after a declaration or ex-post report through a designated foreign exchange bank. The Korean won is not freely convertible outside the onshore system; all corporate KRW funding, dividend remittances, and trade payments must be routed through domestic banks with proper Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS/EFDS) reporting. For a non-resident-owned Yuhan Hoesa in the wholesale cement and vessel freight business, equity contributions are treated as inbound direct investment and are freely convertible after the statutory report and bank verification. Export proceeds from clinker/cement sales may be received in foreign currency and retained onshore, but they must be collected within the statutory export-collection window tied to each export declaration. Profit remittance requires a bank withholding on the dividend, plus confirmation that the domestic entity has filed corporate tax and that the distribution is not classified as a disguised outflow. Capital-account items such as shareholder loans, guarantees, and derivative positions require underlying trade or investment evidence and are subject to bona-fide exposure reviews.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory conversion ratio is applied under current Korean foreign-exchange policy; export collections may be held in a designated foreign-currency account. The statutory collection timeline for general export proceeds is 18 months from the date of export declaration; if vessel freight or bulk clinker delivery timing causes later receipt, the exporter must apply for an extension before the deadline. The full invoice amount must be collected or supported by approved discounts, weight/quality tolerances, or short-delivery/insurance adjustment documentation; any unjustified shortfall will require a formal FEIS explanation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs are not a viable primary rail for Yuhan Hoesa. Korean law reserves the operation of foreign-exchange business and KRW account services to domestic banks and licensed foreign-exchange companies; a foreign EMI with no Korean FETA licence cannot legally open a KRW settlement account, issue corporate cards, or perform FEIS declaration for trade payments. Such EMIs may only support ancillary multi-currency payment products through a domestic partner, but the resulting funds flow would still settle via a domestic bank. Therefore the treasury blueprint excludes fintech EMIs and designates tier-1 domestic banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For Yuhan Hoesa, at least one statutory director and authorised signatory must appear physically in branch for the primary onboarding interview and execution of signature cards, corporate seal registration, and account mandate. Secondary beneficial owners may be verified by recorded video or notarised documents if they are not signatories. Remote consular or notarised power-of-attorney opening is exceptional and is accepted only when the bank can perform physical KYC through its overseas branch; in all cases the bank compliance committee must approve the remote onboarding before any transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unproven provenance of non-resident capital contribution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled or legalised certificate of incorporation, memorandum/articles of association, share register, ownership chart, passing company registry report, audited financial statements or bank reference from the investor jurisdiction, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declaration, and valid passports of each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-flow mismatch in high-volume clinker purchases and freight payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed sale contract, commercial invoice, packing list, original or electronic bill of lading, customs declarations, weight and quality inspection certificates (for example SGS or Bureau Veritas), charter party or freight invoice, cargo insurance policy, and the vessel IMO/sailing route record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and transshipment exposure to restricted ports, particularly for bulk ocean cargo
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed denied-party and sanctions screening report from the bank-linked system, end-user/end-destination certificate, statement from vessel operator confirming no transshipment in prohibited jurisdictions, certificate of origin, insurance certificate, and a legal memorandum opinion on permissibility of the trade route.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent export collection cycle causing potential FEIS reporting breaches
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Aged receivable ledger, debtors confirmation, LC/contract collection schedule, export declaration filings, bank statement reconciliation, freight adjustment or shortage documentation, and a treasury memorandum explaining any discounts or quality-tolerance deductions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity is remitted via SWIFT MT103 to the Yuhan Hoesa capital account at the selected domestic bank. The remitter purpose message must state Equity contribution to Yuhan Hoesa, Republic of Korea; the receiving bank will register the transaction in the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) and, where the contribution exceeds the Foreign Investment Promotion Act threshold, require an FDI declaration reference from MOEF/KOTRA before crediting. The bank then verifies the paid-in amount against the corporate registration and issues a capital receipt/capital verification certificate for the Yuhan Hoesa filing. No third-party collection account, unlicensed EMI, or cash deposit can be used for a compliant capital injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements use SWIFT MT103 or MT202 covers, irrevocable documentary letters of credit under UCP600, or documentary collections under URC 522, depending on the supplier terms. For bulk clinker and cement, an irrevocable sight LC opened by the Korean bank is recommended to protect both seller and buyer. The bank will settle after checking the documents against the LC terms, including B/L, invoice, insurance, inspection certificate, and vessel notification. Trade payments for ocean freight are cleared as service payments through MT103 with the freight invoice and vessel charter party retained in the FEIS file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/KRW forward contracts, available to the entity only when the amount and tenor do not exceed the identified export invoice, import trade payable, or ocean-freight exposure, with the bank reviewed at each rollover.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts, permitted only as a hedge against committed foreign currency flows and only where the domestic bank accepts an NDF structure for a client without the ability to deliver the KRW leg; the notional must be validated by the underlying LC or trade contract.

Cross-currency swaps and interest-rate currency swaps, allowed only where a confirmed corporate loan or structured trade-finance obligation exists in matching currency; speculative or unrelated FX positions will not be approved by the Korean bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Reconciliation Schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year entity, by March 31 of the following year; any approved extension does not postpone the taxable payment due date for base corporate tax.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or underreporting attracts a 20% negligence penalty (40% for fraudulent underreporting) plus delinquency interest on unpaid tax, currently approximately 10.5% per annum; continued non-compliance permits NTS compulsory collection, asset seizure, denial of tax clearance certificates, and for a completely dormant entity, a tax authority request to the registry for administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Enterprise Annual Report and Foreign-Ownership Status Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) / Invest Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the end of the fiscal year; any share transfer, registered capital change, or alteration of controlling foreign shareholders must also be reported within 30 calendar days of the triggering event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may incur an administrative fine up to KRW 3,000,000 (approximately USD 2,300) under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; false reporting may attract criminal sanctions; repeated non-filing can cause loss of foreign-investment protection, banking restrictions, and designation as an inactive entity eligible for judicial dissolution or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Financial Statements and Certified Independent Auditor's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and National Tax Service (NTS); final approval by shareholders at the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For audited companies, the audit report must be delivered in time for the ordinary general meeting held within 3 months after fiscal year-end; the audited financial statements must accompany the corporate tax filing by March 31 for calendar-year entities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, obstruction of the audit or failure to file the auditor's report invalidates the financial statements for statutory purposes and can result in fines up to KRW 200,000,000 (approximately USD 153,000); prolonged failure to file financial statements can lead to compulsory external audit designation, exclusion from credit facilities, and strike-off after dormancy proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Final Returns for Two Six-Month Taxable Periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First taxable period (January 1 through June 30) final return due by July 25 of the same year; second taxable period (July 1 through December 31) final return due by January 25 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing, understatement, or non-payment triggers a 10%-20% negligence penalty, up to 40% for deliberate concealment, and daily delinquency interest; continued non-filing leads to compulsory collection, cancellation of the VAT business registration, and for a dormant entity, an administrative strike-off request to the registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner and Customer Due Diligence KYC Refresh
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Head Office of the Korean banking institution, acting under Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least annually after the Annual General Meeting, and within 30 calendar days of any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to respond to the bank's refresh request can lead to account freezing, transaction restrictions, and a suspicious transaction report to KoFIU; knowingly false confirmation of beneficial ownership constitutes an AML offense punishable by imprisonment and fines, and repeated non-response may cause permanent termination of Korean banking facilities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company) is legally required to appoint a certified public accountant and undergo an independent statutory audit under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if total assets exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,300,000) at the end of the preceding fiscal year. In addition, an audit is mandatory where total assets exceed the lower Presidential Decree threshold of KRW 8,000,000,000 (approximately USD 6,200,000) and annual gross turnover exceeds KRW 30,000,000,000 (approximately USD 23,100,000). Listed entities, public-interest companies, and subsidiaries of audit-designated business groups are also subject to statutory audit regardless of individual entity size. Employment headcount alone does not trigger the audit mandate for a Yuhan Hoesa, but a company with 300 or more employees that is part of a designated audit-target business group is captured through group-level designation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is required for listed and public-interest entities; non-listed companies may apply K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) or Korean SME Accounting Standards where eligible; audits are performed under Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA), which are aligned with IAASB standards, and all financial statements are expressed in Korean Won.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a separate annual UBO registry filing for an ordinary Yuhan Hoesa. The annual confirmation is instead satisfied through three statutory layers: (i) the Foreign Investment Enterprise Annual Report filed with KOTRA/MOTIE within 60 days of fiscal year-end, which identifies foreign shareholders and controlling interests; (ii) the annual beneficial ownership KYC refresh required by the Korean banking institution under FSC/KoFIU AML rules, which must also be refreshed within 30 days of a share transfer; and (iii) a notarized change report to the local corporate registry within 30 days of any transfer of membership shares, accompanied by updating the register of members. A share transfer not recorded in the register of members is unenforceable against third parties under the Commercial Act.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - USD 25,000 per annum when the mandatory audit threshold is exceeded

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9%-24% progressive national corporate income tax; the Korean local income tax surtax is 10% on national corporate tax, producing a combined top marginal rate of 26.4% (24% national plus 2.4% local surtax).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday applies to ISIC 4663 wholesale distribution of cement and bulk clinker. Qualifying foreign investment in Free Economic Zones may obtain a corporate income tax exemption for 3 years and a 50% reduction for the subsequent 2 years under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act. Ordinary preferential deductions include investment tax credits, job-related wage deductions, and foreign tax credits; the statutory foreign investment holiday is generally unavailable to a pure portland-clinker wholesale entity.
